thread:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about switching from the current reservoir/lease model to a "response-budget" approach for soft fairness. TL;DR: budget is per-tenant per-window and decrements by estimated response cost, with carryover limits. Thoughts?
maria: can you sketch the main motivation? is it about latency variance or accounting simplicity?
sam: both. Reservoirs are good for burst shaping but leaks complexity when we try to charge for variable-length responses (multitoken streams). Response-budget ties to token-estimates and lets edge do rough admission.
lee: my worry: abuse surface. With carryover you might get big bursts later. How do we cap scams?
tanvi: add explicit max-burst cap + abuse-score gating. if abuse_score > X then budgets reset slower. do we have telemetry to back this?
josh: telemetry exists but needs extra labels. we should tag admissions with {budget_type, estimated_tokens, client_class, abuse_score} so post-hoc queries can validate model.
sam: agreed. implementation sketch: - AdmitService v2 API: AdmitRequest { tenant_id, est_tokens, route, hints } -> AdmitReply { allowed, reason, lease_ttl, observed_tokens } - allow edge to pass back observed_tokens when stream finishes so we reconcile budgets.
maria: sounds like a breaking API. plan for compatibility?
sam: non-breaking: v1 -> v2 shim in admission sidecar that maps leases to budget reservations, and a dry-run mode flagged via config. rollout path: dry-run -> canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
lee: how about fairness across tenants with long-running streams (chat sessions)? reservoir helped hold capacity for active sessions. budget model might penalize long sessions.
tanvi: we can special-case pinned sessions: assign a reserved sub-budget or convert active_session -> affinity lease that bypasses standard budget for short windows. still need strict SLO for reserved pool.
josh: agree. Also consider KV-cache interplay: cached prefixes reduce real token cost but est_tokens may be high. need edge to provide cache-hit hint so we can lower deduct. maybe AdmitRequest.hints.cache_prefix_match = true.
maria: that opens a new attack vector (fake cache hints). combine with latency / server-side verification heuristics and limit refunds to low-risk clients.
quota-bot: Note: historical peak clients had 3x honest est/actual variance on streaming responses.
sam: good note. For abuse signals, we should feed admit rejections and big refunds into abuse-detector pipeline + create a new "budget-mismatch" metric.
lee: operational cost: threat model suggests we should keep a conservative default: no carryover unless tenant explicitly opted in.
tanvi: also add rollout telemetry dashboards: per-tenant budget burn rate, carryover usage, refunded tokens, budget-mismatch rate.
josh: question about storage: budgets tracked in Redis with per-tenant counters and time-window buckets. switching to budget model increases writes (on stream end) — consider batching or sampling for low-tier traffic.
sam: yep. RFC follow-up action items: 1) draft AdmitService v2 proto & shim plan (owner: sam) 2) telemetry labels and dashboard mockups (owner: josh) 3) abuse gating rules and thresholds (owner: tanvi) 4) migration playbook + feature flagging (owner: maria). I'll open PRs and link here.
maria: +1. I'll coordinate with platform SRE for the canary window.
lee: keep me posted on attack mitigations; I'll run a couple synthetic abuse profiles against the staging shim.
sam: thanks all. I'll post the proto draft by EOD. :rocket:
